tasks.q: What happens when a program contains a syntax error?
a: It will not run: the translator reports the error
It runs but gives the wrong answer
tasks.fb: That is actually helpful: you find out immediately.

tasks.q: Find the syntax error in this program.
tasks.fix: Close the string: print('Running total: ', total)
tasks.fb: A missing quotation mark means the translator cannot tell where the text ends.
tasks.title: Which line breaks the rules?

tasks.q: Find the logic error in this program, which should report a pass at 50 or more.
tasks.fix: Use >= so that a mark of exactly 50 passes
tasks.fb: It runs perfectly and gives the wrong answer for one particular input.
tasks.title: Which line gives the wrong answer?

tasks.q: Why are logic errors harder to find than syntax errors?
a: The program runs without complaint, so nothing points to the mistake
They only happen in long programs
tasks.fb: You have to test carefully to notice the answer is wrong.

tasks.q: Is each mistake a syntax error or a logic error?
items: A loop that runs one time too many

tasks.q: A program outputs 11 when it should output 10. What kind of error is that?
tasks.fb: It ran, so the rules were obeyed.

tasks.q: This program should output the numbers 1 to 5. Find the error.
tasks.fix: The loop variable must match: next i
tasks.fb: The name after next has to be the one the loop counts with.
tasks.title: Which line stops it running?

tasks.q: Why work through a program with a specific input?
a: It shows exactly where what happens stops matching what should happen
It removes the need for testing
tasks.fb: That is what a trace table is for, in the next lesson.

tasks.q: Which is the strongest suggested fix?
a: On line 2, change > to >= so that a mark of exactly 50 passes

tasks.q: This should add up the numbers 1 to 10 but outputs 0. Find the error.
tasks.fb: Every line obeys the rules, so the program runs and prints a confident 0.
tasks.title: Why does it print zero?

tasks.q: This program should print 'Well done' when the score is 10 or more. Find the error.
tasks.fix: Swap the outputs: 'Well done' belongs on the true branch
tasks.fb: The condition is right and the messages are the wrong way round.
tasks.title: Which line has the wrong output?

tasks.q: A question is worth three marks for identifying and correcting an error. What are the three marks likely to be for?
a: The line number, the type of error, and the correction

tasks.q: This program should count down from 5 to 1. Find the error.
tasks.fix: Change n = n + 1 to n = n - 1
tasks.fb: It obeys every rule of the language and never stops running.
tasks.title: Why does it never stop?

tasks.q: Is each mistake a syntax error or a logic error?
items: A loop starting at 0 instead of 1
Testing the lower grade boundary first
tasks.fb: If the translator would object, it is a syntax error.

info.title: The first bug
info.text: In 1947 a moth was found jammed in a relay of the Harvard Mark II. The team taped it into the logbook and called it the first actual case of a bug being found.

info.title: Syntax errors are the friendly ones
info.text: They stop the program immediately and tell you roughly where. Logic errors can survive into released software for years.

info.title: Off by one
info.text: Loops that run one time too many or too few are so common they have their own name: off-by-one errors.

info.title: Runtime errors
info.text: There is a third kind: errors that appear only while running, such as dividing by zero. At GCSE the focus is syntax and logic.

info.title: Rubber ducking
info.text: Programmers explain their code line by line to an inanimate object to find logic errors. It works surprisingly often.

info.title: Exam tip
info.text: Always give the line number. Describing the error without locating it usually loses a mark.
